# Review #354

**Result: block.** Exact head `d5813cada7341fbda7f2816c3d6679f48800db4f`, compared with its parent/main `387362db777476a26a789f9e5e15b356e046cc6b`. One reviewer, one round under amended C34. The three blocks are false instructions or descriptions of normal-use behavior, not requests to harden the pod implementation.

## Findings

**B354-R1-01 -- block: the advertised views require JSON.**
`docs/cli/pods.md:48-55,86` documents ordinary `pod show` as displaying the member model, owner holders, deliverable stages and log, and promises a closed pod reads `closed`. Ordinary `pod sessions` is also said to show session transcripts. The daemon supplies those fields, but the text renderer drops them. An actual binary built from the private exact-head archive, against a synthetic local HTTP fixture, returned all these fields with `--json` and omitted them without it; a closed pod with a working keep-open knowledge member printed no pod state at all. `crates/cli/src/main.rs:2306-2315` selects that renderer; `crates/cli/src/pod.rs:56-95,140-153,186-219` omits the fields. Document `--json` for the full views and qualify what ordinary text displays. This docs-only repair is sufficient; no unrelated rendering feature is requested. `activity` likewise prints transcript locations, not transcript contents.

**B354-R1-02 -- block: unfiltered history does not include every seat.**
`docs/cli/pods.md:55` says `pij sessions --history` lists history "for every seat". Without `--seat`, `crates/daemon/src/http/shim.rs:113-118` explicitly excludes tombstoned seats. A closed seat's history remains available when named with `--seat <id>`; `pod sessions` also names its recorded members individually. Say "all non-tombstoned seats" and give the explicit-seat command for closed seats.

**B354-R1-03 -- block: the no-start joining command is unported.**
`docs/cli/pods.md:39` instructs `pij spawn --as role:<id>[/<instance>] --pod <pod>`. The shim's spawn route always refuses `E-RS-UNPORTED` (`.omp/extensions/pij/core/generation-routing.ts:371-374`). The deployed command, safely probed with `--help`, reproduced that refusal. Native `pij-rs spawn --help` confirms `--as` and `--pod` are supported, with the role's harness used when omitted. Change this example to `pij-rs spawn --as role:<id>[/<instance>] --pod <pod>`.

**B354-R1-04 -- nonblocking state note.**
PRD 009 req-05's listing criterion is satisfied: all first pages, including pods, are bundled. Workstream 009 s03 is marked complete and adds a dependency on 008 s02, but `docs/project/workstreams/008-pods.dd.json:39-41` still marks s02 in-progress at this head. The pod behavior is on main in #346; acknowledge the outstanding prerequisite or reconcile its state against actual completion receipts, rather than treating "merged" as an existing complete-state receipt.

## Coverage and validation

All 11 pod verbs and their documented flags were checked against the deployed help and the unchanged main implementation. Template paths are caller-relative, never searched; template/parameter integrity refusals are distinct from advisory checks. The secret guard precedes pod parameter writes. The canary uses one subscription and a single 15-minute deadline; a later member confirmation recovers a degraded slot. The degraded check is a **one-directional safety brake**, not a policy: removing it only sends more. It skips `set` to degraded members and write-back when any live destination holder is a degraded member of this pod; other sends are untouched. Down uses one git status read, the existing close-stop handler per non-keep-open member, and never touches consulted roles. History reads at most 256 KiB per listed session and reports `unknown` when unavailable; the page should mention that qualification. PRD 010 procedures and shipped templates are clearly Coming.
